content.text: {"label":"system_slowness","explanation":"Handle time rose sharply in both queues from 12:00. Payments went from about 300 s to 561 s and general from about 350 s to 486 s. A P2 incident opened at 12:15 reports core banking screens freezing, with account-summary API latency above 8 s. Volume is near forecast: payments is +0.2% for the day and general is -10%. The call-reason mix is close to normal, and absences (2 and 3) are at or below usual levels. Fewer agents on phones (36 vs 38 planned) adds a little pressure but is not the driver. The cause is supply lost to slow systems, not extra demand or a customer-facing outage.","plan_name":"Core-banking slowness: protect both queues with free levers, overtime and digital offload","rationale":"Both queues are breaching (payments 2.2%, general 26.9% at 12:15), so neither can donate agents and moving cross-skilled staff is ruled out. An outage message is not appropriate because customers are not calling about a known fault. The plan has four parts. First, the free levers: delay breaks on both queues and turn on callbacks for both queues to soften peaks. Second, cancel coaching to bring agents back to the phones. Third, add capacity through overtime, starting at 13:00 because agents arrive 30 min after approval. The expected overtime cost assumes 40% acceptance. Payments offer 1 (20 agents, 13:00-15:00): about 8 accept, 16 h, Rs 5,760. General offer (12 agents, 13:00-15:00): about 5 accept, 10 h, Rs 3,600. Payments offer 2 (10 agents, 15:00-17:00, in case the incident runs on): about 4 accept, 8 h, Rs 2,880. That totals about Rs 12,240, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Fourth, shift eligible simple enquiries to chat. On payments this is payment_status_enquiry and refund_status, roughly 150 chats or about Rs 1,800. On general it is balance_enquiry, roughly 40 chats or about Rs 500. Review at the next interval and when the vendor reports on the incident; stand down overtime if handle time returns to
